findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext long-lived credentials. User data is readable from the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the internet-facing web server), through ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and is stored unencrypted in Terraform state.

The instance sits in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true routed to an internet gateway, behind a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on 22 and 80, and defines no metadata_options with http_tokens = "required". IMDSv1 therefore remains available, so an SSRF or any local process can read the metadata service and the plaintext credentials in user data.
No root_block_device (or ebs_block_device) block sets encrypted = true, so the instance root volume may be created without encryption at rest depending on the AMI and account default.
Ingress allows TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the public instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, imposing no outbound boundary and easing data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the bootstrap script configures Apache to serve plain HTTP with no TLS listener, so all traffic to the web host is transmitted in cleartext.

The EBS volume attached to the web host omits encrypted = true (it is explicitly commented out), so data at rest on the volume is unencrypted unless account-level default encryption happens to be enabled.

The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and configures no encryption, so this point-in-time copy of the data is stored unencrypted and can be copied or shared without cryptographic protection.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network telemetry — a valuable reconnaissance source — is stored without enforced encryption at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, restrictive bucket policy, or TLS-only (aws:SecureTransport) policy is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public ACL/policy grants and to access over unencrypted transport.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the associated route table's 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, makes every instance launched here — including the web host — directly internet-addressable with no NAT or bastion boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway make any workload placed in this subnet internet-facing by default.
